experience.role: Full Stack Software Engineer, Real-Time Operations
highlights: Own the rules domain end-to-end within Axon’s Real-Time Alerts platform, spanning data modelling, APIs, real-time evaluation, operator tooling, and cloud operations for a platform available to approximately 20,000 agencies and more than 1 million users globally.

Built a low-latency rule engine in Go that evaluates real-time events against agency-defined alert rules across a platform processing more than 400 million events annually, applying role, proximity, and permission conditions while delivering alerts with p99 latency under 1.5 seconds.

Designed the rules data model and REST APIs and built the operator-facing Rule Editor in Angular, providing end-to-end lifecycle management for creating, updating, enabling, disabling, and deleting alert rules.
Provision and operate cloud-native services on AKS using Terraform, Helm, ArgoCD, and Istio, with gRPC/Protobuf for inter-service communication, maintaining 99.99% availability for the rules domain.
Mentor junior engineers through system design, code reviews, debugging, and implementation, helping them take ownership of production services and reinforcing team engineering standards.

Use Cursor, Claude, and Codex to accelerate repository-wide implementation, refactoring, test generation, debugging, and code review, validating generated changes through automated testing and peer review.

Designed, built, and deployed a Java/Spring service to production within four months, processing more than 1 million social-platform messages to identify customer-exposed sensitive data, including payment card information and confidential files.
Built automated detection and triage workflows that surfaced high-confidence exposures to customers for investigation and streamlined downstream takedown requests.
Implemented the event-driven service using Spring, RabbitMQ, and Docker and provisioned its AWS infrastructure, including S3 and EC2, using Terraform.
Built and shipped a production system mapping 75% of logical and physical data flows across NatWest Markets’ application estate.
Presented the system and findings to senior leadership, including the CTO.

projects.name: Evaluating Language Models for Frame Identification in News Articles
projects.stack: Python, PyTorch, Scikit-Learn, NumPy, Pandas, Hugging Face
highlights: Built two NLP models using Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis to identify media frames in news articles, achieving a 10% improvement in precision and recall over the state of the art at the time.
Submitted findings for publication, contributing to research in automated frame identification.
